page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 63.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU configuration includes a 32 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It features dedicated CPU allocation and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4d-highmem-8 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng single-core CPU score of 3451.09 and high single-threaded compression throughput, reaching 37.91 GB/sec in gzip and 16.87 GB/sec in bzip3. Multi-core and memory subsystem performance generally align with mid-range expectations, with a multi-core stress-ng score of 13798.02 and uncached memory read bandwidth of 49.49 GB/sec. For machine learning tasks, the instance achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 373.98 tokens/sec on small 135M models, though prompt processing speeds drop to the bottom 25% when scaling up to medium 7B models.

From a resource density perspective, the c4d-highmem-8 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of nearly 8 GB per core, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel compute scaling. The lack of bundled local storage means storage-heavy applications must rely on external network-attached storage, which introduces a latency tradeoff. This instance is well-suited for database operations, Redis caching layers, single-threaded data processing pipelines, and lightweight language model inference.

Powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor with 4 physical cores and hyperthreading, it features a 32 MB L3 cache and supports AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks highlight top-tier single-core capabilities, including high single-threaded compression speeds and efficient text generation for small language models, while multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics remain average. This profile makes the c4d-highmem-8 highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, caching systems like Redis, and single-threaded data processing tasks that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation without requiring local storage.
